newsitem.title: USA: Clinton widens his leads in Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: Clinton widens his leads in Reuters poll.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Thursday widened his lead over Republican Bob Dole in the Reuters daily tracking poll to 13.3 percentage points as he dominated the air waves by hosting a Middle East summit.
The survey of 962 likely voters, conducted by John Zogby Group International, is a rolling average of polling results from Monday through Wednesday and carries a 3.3 percentage point margin of error.
Clinton led by 46.2 percent to Dole's 32.9 percent. Reform Party candidate Ross Perot trailed with 4.6 percent.
That represented an improvement of 2.7 percentage points for Clinton in the past 24 hours and the president's best rating since the daily poll began on Tuesday.

Clinton has dominated the news headlines in the past two days, hosting a Middle East summit that produced an agreement by Israel and the Palestinians to resume peace talks but no substantive progress.
"Stated simply, Bill Clinton had a huge day on Tuesday, probably as a result of all the publicity surrounding the Middle East summit," said pollster John Zogby.
Dole criticised Clinton for conducting "photo-op diplomacy" but has found it difficult to make his voice heard.
The next big event of the campaign comes Sunday, exactly one month before Election Day, when the candidates square off in the first of two presidential debates.
The jump in Clinton's support did not translate into support for Democrats running for Congress, where the two parties remained locked in a virtual dead heat.
Asked which party's candidate they intended to vote for in their congressional district, 35.3 percent of respondents said Democrat and 34.6 percent said Republican.

Clinton's surge was particularly noticeable in the Midwest and Great Lakes states and the president leads among women by 50 percent to 27.7 percent. Among men, his lead is less than three percentage points.
